bull.argument: The filing shows strong momentum. Total net sales rose 15% to $478,834 million, with iPhone up 21% and Services up 13% to $123,301 million. Services carries a 76.2% gross margin, which helps lift the total gross margin percentage to 48.8% from 46.9%. Management also has substantial financial capacity: it reports $136.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, and it returned capital at scale in 2026. The bear case is real, and the filing says so. Management expects gross margins to face "volatility and downward pressure," memory and storage costs are rising, tariffs remain uncertain, and R&D jumped 32%. But the mix shift toward high-margin Services and a large cash base give Apple room to absorb these pressures while still investing in AI and returning capital to shareholders.

claims.claim: Services revenue grew 13% and is a high-margin growth driver supporting overall margins.
claims.quote: Services net sales increased during 2026 compared to 2025 primarily due to higher net sales from advertising and cloud services.

claims.claim: The company returned substantial capital to shareholders in 2026.
claims.quote: During 2026, the Company repurchased $85.8 billion of its common stock and paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $15.7 billion.

claims.claim: The company holds a large liquidity cushion to fund operations and capital returns.
claims.quote: which totaled $136.9 billion as of September 26, 2026

bear.argument: The bull case leans on a strong 2026, but the filing signals that the current margin profile is fragile. Management states that gross margins "will be subject to volatility and downward pressure," and it expects memory and storage cost pressures to "intensify." The 2026 products margin gain of 39.3% was attributed partly to "tariff refunds," a one-time type of benefit tied to a Supreme Court ruling, not durable operating improvement. Meanwhile, R&D rose 32% to $45,765 million, and the filing links this to "higher infrastructure-related costs, including investments in artificial intelligence," with returns not guaranteed. The company also faces tariff uncertainty, with the filing warning that the "ultimate impact remains uncertain." Greater China sales swung from a 4% decline to a 28% increase, showing sensitivity to a single region. Finally, the company is spending heavily on buybacks, $85.8 billion, while manufacturing purchase obligations reach $89.7 billion, with $82.7 billion due within 12 months. That commits cash to supply that management says faces constraints. Strong recent results may not persist under these pressures.

claims.claim: Management expects gross margins to face downward pressure, undermining the sustainability of the 48.8% margin.
claims.quote: the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure

claims.claim: Part of the 2026 products margin improvement came from tariff refunds, which may not recur.
claims.quote: primarily due to product mix and tariff refunds, partially offset by higher costs, including memory

claims.claim: R&D spending jumped 32% with returns on AI investment not assured.
claims.quote: These investments may not achieve expected returns

bull.argument: The bear case is fair on risks but overstates fragility. Yes, management expects gross margins to face "volatility and downward pressure," and tariff refunds helped the 2026 products margin. But the filing is explicit that refunds were recognized as a reduction of product cost of sales, and it attributes the products margin gain "primarily" to product mix as well as refunds, so mix is a durable driver, not just a one-time item. Services, the higher-margin business, grew 13% and its gross margin rose to 76.2%. On R&D, the 32% increase is tied to AI and infrastructure, which the filing treats as a deliberate investment. Yes, spending is heavy, but the company reports $136.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and states this is sufficient for its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond. The $82.7 billion in manufacturing obligations is large, but it is a supply commitment funded by an operating business that generated $478.8 billion in sales. The risks are real; the financial base to absorb them is also real.

claims.claim: Management attributes the products margin gain primarily to product mix, not only tariff refunds.
claims.quote: Products gross margin and gross margin percentage increased during 2026 compared to 2025 primarily due to product mix and tariff refunds

claims.claim: Services gross margin percentage rose, supporting overall profitability.
claims.quote: Services gross margin percentage increased during 2026 compared to 2025 primarily due to a different mix of services

claims.claim: Management states its cash balances are sufficient for cash requirements and capital returns over the next 12 months and beyond.
claims.quote: will be sufficient to satisfy its cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond

bear.argument: The opponent concedes the risks but argues mix is durable and cash is ample. Yet the filing does not say mix is durable; it says products margin rose "primarily due to product mix and tariff refunds," and refunds are a non-recurring benefit from a Supreme Court ruling on tariffs that were struck down. Management's own outlook is that gross margins "will be subject to volatility and downward pressure," and it expects memory and storage cost pressures to "intensify." Services is strong, but its 76.2% margin rose partly from "a different mix of services," and the filing ties services cost increases to "higher costs" too. On cash, the $136.9 billion balance is set against $89.7 billion of manufacturing purchase obligations, $82.7 billion due within 12 months, and $85.8 billion of buybacks in 2026. Those commitments plus shareholder returns absorb most of the liquidity the company cites. The R&D increase of 32% is described as an investment whose "returns" may not be achieved, and the filing says new products "may produce lower revenue and lower profit margins." The base is real, but it is being fully deployed.

claims.claim: Management expects gross margins to face downward pressure, so the 48.8% margin may not hold.
claims.quote: the Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure

claims.claim: The 2026 products margin gain was partly driven by tariff refunds, a benefit that may not recur.
claims.quote: primarily due to product mix and tariff refunds, partially offset by higher costs, including memory

claims.claim: R&D rose 32% but the filing says these investments may not achieve expected returns.
claims.quote: These investments may not achieve expected returns

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes, so evidence is roughly even. The bear better answers the bull's Round 2 claim that mix is durable by pointing out that the filing lists mix and refunds together and ties the margin gain to a non-recurring benefit, and it weighs cash commitments against buybacks more concretely. The bull's point that the cash base is sufficient is credible, but it does not fully address the bear's argument that the liquidity is largely committed.
